arxiv-2201-05486.title: A computational framework for modelling infectious disease policy based on
arxiv-2201-05486.creator: age and household structure with applications to the COVID-19 pandemic
arxiv-2201-05486.description: Abstract Abstract The widespread, and in many countries unprecedented, use of non-pharmaceutical interventions during the COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the need for mathematical models which can estimate the impact of these measures while accounting for the highly heterogeneous risk profile of COVID-19.

arxiv-2305-16876.title: CombLM: Adapting Black-Box Language Models through Small Fine-Tuned Models
arxiv-2305-16876.creator: Aitor Ormazabal, Mikel Artetxe, Eneko Agirre
arxiv-2305-16876.description: Abstract Methods for adapting language models (LMs) to new tasks and domains have traditionally assumed white-box access to the model, and work by modifying its parameters. However, this is incompatible with a recent trend in the field, where the highest quality models are only available as black-boxes through inference APIs.

arxiv-2306-16509.title: Hydrodynamics of thermally-driven chiral propulsion and separation
arxiv-2306-16509.creator: E. Kirkinis, A. V. Andreev, M. Olvera de la Cruz
arxiv-2306-16509.description: Abstract Considerable effort has been directed towards the characterization of chiral mesoscale structures, as shown in chiral protein assemblies and carbon nanotubes. Here, we establish a thermally-driven hydrodynamic description for the actuation and separation of mesoscale chiral structures in a fluid medium.

arxiv-2308-14923.title: Well-posed problem for a combustion model in a multilayer porous medium
arxiv-2308-14923.creator: Marcos R. Batista, Alysson Cunha, Jesus C. Da Mota, Ronaldo A. Santos
arxiv-2308-14923.description: Abstract Combustion occurring in porous media has various practical applications, such as in in-situ combustion processes in oil reservoirs, the combustion of biogas in sanitary landfills, and many others. A porous medium where combustion takes place can consist of layers with different physical properties.

arxiv-2404-06628.title: Quantum graph models for transport in filamentary switching
arxiv-2404-06628.creator: Alison A. Silva, Fabiano M. Andrade, Francesco Caravelli
arxiv-2404-06628.description: Abstract The formation of metallic nanofilaments bridging two electrodes across an insulator is a mechanism for resistive switching. Examples of such phenomena include atomic synapses, which constitute a distinct class of memristive devices whose behavior is closely tied to the properties of the filament. Until recently, experimental investigation of the low-temperature regime and quantum transport effects has been limited.

pmc-10574613.title: Effectiveness of Fish Roe, Snow Fungus, and Yeast Supplementation for Cognitive Function: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial
pmc-10574613.creator: Yung-Kai Lin, Yung-Hsiang Lin, Chi-Fu Chiang, Li Jingling, Antonios Dakanalis
pmc-10574613.description: The brain is one of the most critical organs in the human body, regulating functions such as thinking, memory, learning, and perception. Studies have indicated that fish roe, snow fungus, and yeast may have the potential to modulate cognitive, memory, and emotional functions. However, more relevant clinical research in this area still needs to be conducted.

pmc-10629733.title: Predicting hepatic encephalopathy in patients with cirrhosis: A UK population–based study and validation of risk scores
pmc-10629733.creator: Bethan I Jones, Cerys A Jenkins, Daniel Murphy, James Orr, Andrew Yeoman, Ellen R Hubbuck, Ben R Heywood, Craig J Currie
pmc-10629733.description: Background:HE is a common neurologic complication in cirrhosis associated with substantial disease and economic burden. HE symptoms are nonspecific and there are limited ways of identifying patients with cirrhosis at high risk of later developing HE. A risk score was previously developed to identify patients at risk of developing HE in a predominately male US cohort.

pmc-10727383.title: The EVA (Early Vascular Aging) Study: Association of Central Obesity With Worse Arterial Health After Preeclampsia
pmc-10727383.creator: Amélie Paquin, Ana Werlang, Thais Coutinho
pmc-10727383.description: BackgroundWomen with preeclampsia have a higher risk of cardiovascular disease. This is partly explained by the worse arterial health after preeclampsia. Central obesity (CO) is a risk factor for both preeclampsia and cardiovascular disease. Whether CO contributes to further worsening of arterial health after preeclampsia remains unclear.

pmc-11432617.title: Distinct Genomic Expression Signatures after Low-Force Electrically Induced Exercises in Persons with Spinal Cord Injury
pmc-11432617.creator: Michael A Petrie, Manish Suneja, Richard K Shields, Sebastien Couillard-Despres
pmc-11432617.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). People with a spinal cord injury are at an increased risk of metabolic dysfunction due to skeletal muscle atrophy and the transition of paralyzed muscle to a glycolytic, insulin-resistant phenotype. Providing doses of exercise through electrical muscle stimulation may provide a therapeutic intervention to help restore metabolic function for people with a spinal cord injury, but high-frequency and high-force electrically induced muscle contractions increase fracture risk for the underlying osteoporotic skeletal system.

pmc-11511143.title: Endosomal pH, Redox Dual-Sensitive Prodrug Micelles Based on Hyaluronic Acid for Intracellular Camptothecin Delivery and Active Tumor Targeting in Cancer Therapy
pmc-11511143.creator: Huiping Zhang, Liang Li, Wei Li, Hongxia Yin, Huiyun Wang, Xue Ke
pmc-11511143.description: Background: CPT is a pentacyclic monoterpene alkaloid with a wide spectrum of antitumor activity. Its clinical application is restricted due to poor water solubility, instability, and high toxicity. We developed a new kind of multifunctional micelles to improve its solubility, reduce the side effecs, and obtain enhanced antitumor effects.

pmc-12375940.title: Maternal Exposure to Medications and the Risk of Congenital and Early‐Onset Hearing Loss in Children: A Systematic Review and a Meta‐Analysis
pmc-12375940.creator: Asli Sena Kücükyildiz, Mette Østergaard Thunbo, Christer Zøylner Swan, David P Burgner, Jessica E Miller, Therese Ovesen, Lars Henning Pedersen
pmc-12375940.description: BackgroundCongenital hearing loss (CHL) affects approximately 1–2 in 1000 children and significantly impacts development. Exposure to medications during pregnancy may impact offspring hearing; however, the ototoxic effects of different drugs have not been systematically investigated.MethodsThis systematic review and meta‐analysis was conducted following PRISMA guidelines and analysed 21 experimental and observational studies examining 60 drugs across various categories.

pmc-12468341.title: Adaptation and Vulnerability in Chronic Pain: A Study of Profiles Based on Clinical and Psychological Factors
pmc-12468341.creator: Juan José Mora-Ascó, Carmen Moret-Tatay, María José Jorques-Infante, María José Beneyto-Arrojo
pmc-12468341.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Chronic pain (CP) is a multidimensional condition that exerts a considerable impact on individuals’ quality of life and presents a wide range of clinical and psychological expressions. This study sought, firstly, to identify distinct clinical profiles among individuals with CP based on clinical indicators, and secondly, to examine the differences in psychological vulnerability and pain-related coping strategies according to the clinical profiles. A total of 251 adults diagnosed with CP and residing in Spain participated in the study.

pmc-13184019.title: Estimation of the effective dose in torso 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT: an analysis of real-world clinical data from 51,784 patient scans
pmc-13184019.creator: Jeongryul Ryu, Jungsu S. Oh, Yong-il Kim, Sangwon Han, Jae Seung Kim, Kyung-Hyun Do, Jin-Sook Ryu
pmc-13184019.description: BackgroundLarge-scale estimation of effective dose (ED) for positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT) remains limited. This study aimed to determine the ED of torso 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT using extensive real-world clinical data from a high-volume centre. Differences in ED were also evaluated according to PET/CT scanner type, patient sex, and body size.

pmc-13662887.title: Nudix hydrolase 15 deficiency and azathioprine toxicity in a liver transplant recipient: A case report
pmc-13662887.creator: Jenny Q. Nguyen, Natalie Rodriguez, Kimberly A. Chapman, Matthew A. Deardorff, Keith Z. Hazleton
pmc-13662887.description: Thiopurines, such as azathioprine (AZA), are among the immunosuppressants used to prevent allograft rejection. Thiopurines are metabolized by thiopurine S‐methyltransferase (TPMT) and nudix hydrolase 15 (NUDT15) enzymes, and their functions are highly influenced by genetic variation. We present a 6‐year‐old female with recurrent acute cellular rejection and steroid‐induced glaucoma due to high‐dose corticosteroid therapy.
